plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single-trace ultraviolet absorption spectrum of 1,3-butadiene plotted over a pink gradient field. The vertical axis is labeled "Absorbance", carries a magenta arrow pointing up beside the label, and runs from 0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks every 0.2. The horizontal axis reads "Wavelength (nm)", is followed by a magenta arrow pointing right, and spans 200 to 400 with labeled ticks every 20 nm. One magenta curve enters at the left edge near 0.34, climbs steeply to a rounded maximum just under 0.9 at about 215 nm, then falls sharply through 240 nm to roughly 0.07, after which it declines almost imperceptibly along a near-horizontal tail to about 0.03 at the right edge. A short annotation just above and right of the crest reads "lambda max = 217 nm". With the zero baseline at the bottom of the chart rather than the top, absorption registers as a peak rising off a flat floor, and the eye is meant to fix on that lone crest against the featureless tail beyond 250 nm. The trace records the wavelength of strongest absorption for a simple conjugated diene, the reading from which molar absorptivity is calculated.

interactionPlan.concept: A UV absorption spectrum identifies λmax as the wavelength where a compound absorbs most strongly, with 1,3-butadiene showing its diagnostic maximum near 217 nm and only weak absorption at longer wavelengths.

interactions.label: Wavelength
interactions.teaches: λmax is not just the tallest point on the drawing; it is the wavelength value where the absorbance readout reaches its highest value as the spectrum is scanned

interactions.label: View focus
interactions.teaches: The important UV signal for 1,3-butadiene is concentrated near the short-wavelength peak, while the long-wavelength tail contributes little absorbance

demo_steps.title: Find the maximum
demo_steps.narration: Start with the marker at the crest of the magenta curve. The absorbance readout is highest near 217 nm, so this wavelength is labeled λmax.

demo_steps.title: Scan away from the crest
demo_steps.narration: Move the wavelength slider to the right and watch the dot drop rapidly down the curve. The absorbance falls sharply after the maximum, showing why nearby wavelengths are not λmax.

demo_steps.title: Compare the long tail
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the full-tail view and scan through longer wavelengths. Beyond about 250 nm, the curve is nearly flat and close to the baseline, so the diagnostic absorption is the short-wavelength peak rather than the tail.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: λmax is the wavelength at the highest absorbance point, and for 1,3-butadiene that point is the isolated peak near 217 nm rather than the weak long-wavelength tail.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the figure as a clean 2D line plot with a pale pink gradient filling the plotting rectangle, darkest near the top and fading toward white near the bottom. Use black axes and ticks, serif-style tick labels, and a bright magenta trace. The curve should begin near moderate absorbance at 200 nm, rise steeply to a smooth rounded crest near 217 nm just under 0.9, fall quickly by about 240 nm, then continue as a very low, gently declining tail to 400 nm. Place the 'λmax = 217 nm' annotation just above and to the right of the crest. In Peak-only mode, visually emphasize the peak with a subtle glow or shaded band around 217 nm while de-emphasizing the tail; in Full-tail mode, show the whole curve and lightly highlight the low tail beyond about 250 nm. The slider marker should be a small high-contrast dot riding exactly on the curve with a compact live readout such as 'λ = 217 nm, A ≈ 0.86'.

authoredContext:
Note that UV spectra differ from IR spectra in how they are presented. For historical reasons, IR spectra are usually displayed so that the baseline corresponding to zero absorption runs across the top of the chart and a valley indicates an absorption, whereas UV spectra are displayed with the baseline at the bottom of the chart so that a peak indicates an absorption (the figure).

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene, λmax = 217 nm.

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene shows a peak at (217, 0.85) where lambda max equals 217 nanometers. The x-axis and y-axis represent wavelength and absorbance, respectively.

discrepancies: The default plot includes a white/magenta circular marker and a floating readout box at the peak, neither of which appears in the source figure.

The generated figure adds vertical pink highlight bands around the peak and a pale overlay/faded tail region, while the source has only a smooth pink gradient background and a uniformly magenta curve.

The plotted spectrum is noticeably compressed horizontally relative to the wide source figure because the UI panel occupies a large portion of the rendered width, making the peak look narrower and steeper at a glance.
The curve shape is close but not exact: the generated peak is slightly shifted/rounded and the post-peak decay appears too abrupt with a lower tail around 235–250 nm than in the source.
The λmax label is rendered as plain 'λmax = 217 nm' rather than using the subscript styling shown in the source, and it is placed slightly closer to the curve than the original.
The magenta x-direction arrow is smaller and positioned farther below the x-axis label than in the source, and the y-direction arrow is shorter than the original.
evaluation.notes: The axes, main magenta UV spectrum, gradient background, and λmax annotation are recognizable, but the default view is cluttered by non-source interactive overlays and has a noticeably altered aspect and curve emphasis.
action_items: Remove or hide the marker dot, readout box, and highlight bands in the default state so the initial rendering matches the static source figure.
Keep the curve uniformly bright magenta across the full wavelength range unless the user explicitly activates an explanatory focus mode.
Use a wider plot aspect ratio closer to the source image so the spectrum is not visually compressed by the side UI panel.
Adjust the absorbance curve to better match the source decay, especially the shoulder/tail between about 230 and 260 nm, and format λmax with a proper subscript.
plan_action_items: Make the source-matching static figure the default state, with scanning/readout/focus overlays introduced only through an explicit interaction or demo step.

feedback.rationale: The core concept and interactions are correct, but the default rendering has implementation-level hallucinated overlays, aspect-ratio compression, curve/label styling issues, and default-state fixes best handled by the generator.
